newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end flat amid market uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end flat amid market uncertainty.

text.p: Swedish shares closed lower on Wednesday after a day of mixed trade with the Stockholm bourse shrugging off gains in New York and U.S. data adding a dash of uncertainty.
The Stockholm general index ended 0.05 percent percent higher at 2,667.20 after rising strongly on Tuesday.
Shares worth 3.93 billion crowns changed hands.
"The stronger-than-expected U.S. figures (for industrial production and capacity utilization) proved that there is a lot of uncertainty in the market," one broker said.
A winner of the day was lock maker Assa Abloy.
It jumped 19 crowns to 170 crowns after anouncing it was buying French lock making group Vachette for 1.1 billion francs. The purchase would be partly funded by a rights issue.
Tools and speciality maker SKF continued to post losses after reporting a 38 percent drop in first quarter profits on Tuesday. It closed nine crowns lower at 166.5.

State-controlled bank Nordbanken closed 7.5 higher at 259.5 crowns. The Swedish government said its supplementary budget released on Tuesday included the sale of state Nordbanken shares worth 17 billion crowns.
